title: Staging target check
issueTitle: Staging target check compares folder strings, not resolved paths
function: The deploy workflow's `Check staging target` step, in `.github/workflows/deploy-spaceship.yml`, is meant to refuse a staging folder that is the production folder or the FTP root, but it compares the two folders as strings with only their leading and trailing slashes normalised. A staging folder that names the production folder another way therefore passes, and a manual run with `clean_staging` set would then delete the production site. This fix makes the step compare resolved paths: it resolves the `.` and `..` segments of both folders and refuses a staging folder that resolves to the production folder or to the FTP root.

gap.summary: The staging target check compares folder strings, not resolved paths. Its `normalize` helper only adds a leading and a trailing slash, so `.` and `..` segments stay as written and a staging folder that names the production folder another way is not refused. The production folder is configured as `/../../spartanlaboratories.org/` (#9), so a staging folder set to `/spartanlaboratories.org/` passes, and a manual run with `clean_staging` set would delete everything in it: the production site. A staging folder that resolves to the FTP root but is not written `/`, such as `/../`, passes the root test the same way.
gap.detail: At the baseline the step stands at lines 106-126 of the workflow; the issue cites lines 99-111. The docs publish already compares resolved paths in its own target check.
evidence: `.github/workflows/deploy-spaceship.yml:112-116` — `normalize` adds a leading and a trailing slash and resolves no `.` or `..` segment
`.github/workflows/deploy-spaceship.yml:121-124` — the step fails only when the staging string is `/` or equals the production string
`.github/workflows/deploy-spaceship.yml:181` — the staging deploy passes the manual run's `clean_staging` input on as `clean-remote`
`.github/actions/spaceship-deploy/action.yml:38-39`, `:139` — `clean-remote` deletes everything in the remote folder before uploading
`.github/workflows/publish-docs.yml:51-53` — the docs publish compares paths resolved with `realpath -m`, noting that the production folder is configured as `/../../spartanlaboratories.org/`

statements.text: The step resolves both folders with a `resolve` function that applies their `.` and `..` segments, keeps a `..` at the root at the root and collapses repeated slashes, and compares the results.

It refuses a staging folder that resolves to the FTP root and one that resolves to the production folder, each with its own `::error::` annotation naming `SPACESHIP_STAGING_REMOTE_DIR`, and exits before it writes `remote_dir`.
`resolve` reads the folders as text in bash; no `realpath` or other tool is called.
The step writes the resolved staging folder as `remote_dir`, the output `Deploy to staging` reads; a folder written plainly, as the default is, comes out as before.

verdict.defense: A fix to one step of one workflow, with the test that runs that step as committed. Resolving the folders from their text gives the step the meaning of the documents publish's check without depending on the runner, so the test runs exactly the code the runner runs. Handing on the resolved folder makes what was checked what is uploaded to, and for the live default the two are the same. The production job, the documents publish and the shared deploy action are untouched.

risks: The step is the only guard in front of the manual clean option: a mistake in its resolving could refuse the live configuration, which stops the staging job before anything is uploaded, or accept a folder it should refuse; the tests cover the issue's case, its spellings, the root and the live configuration

A staging folder written with `.`, `..`, repeated slashes or no leading slash now uploads to the folder it resolves to; no staging variable is set and the default is written plainly, so the live upload folder does not change

The check assumes the FTP host reads a `..` at its root as the root, as `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` records and production deploys through today; were it otherwise, production would be set to its plain spelling, which the check reads as before
Folder names are compared as written and case matters: a host that ignored case would let a spelling of production that differs only in case pass as a separate folder
A production folder that resolves to the root is not judged by the staging check; the production job's own check is a follow-up

options.name: Resolve the folders in bash from their text
options.summary: A short function in the step applies the `.` and `..` segments and collapses repeated slashes.
options.wins: It consults nothing on the runner, needs no tool, and gives the same answers in the test's bash as on the runner.

options.name: Match the documents publish with `realpath -m`
options.why: It resolves symbolic links on the runner's file system, which means nothing for an FTP folder, and some builds keep a leading `//` as a root of its own, so the check and its test would disagree across machines.
options.summary: Resolve both folders with `realpath -m`, as the documents publish does in its own target check.

options.name: `realpath -ms` with the leading slashes stripped first
options.why: It gives the same answers on every folder tried, but adds a tool and a flag to a guard that needs neither.
options.summary: Strip the folders' leading slashes, then resolve them with `realpath -ms`.

options.name: Compare resolved paths but upload to the folder as written
options.why: What was checked would not be what is uploaded to: the host would read a spelling the check had already read differently.
options.summary: Compare the resolved folders, but hand the staging folder to the deploy as it is written.

options.name: Also refuse a staging folder that contains production or the documents folder
options.why: The issue asks for equal or root only. For the live production folder the root is the only ancestor and is refused; the rest is a follow-up with its own test.
options.summary: Refuse a resolved staging folder that is a proper ancestor of the resolved production folder or of the documents folder, with a test for each.

followUps.note: `Check production target` refuses a production folder only when its text is `/`, so `/..` or `/a/..` would pass and send the site into the FTP root. Resolving the folder with the same function and refusing the root closes it, with a test beside the staging one.

The staging check still accepts a proper ancestor of production and a folder that contains the documents folder. For the live production folder the only proper ancestor is the FTP root, which is refused; a production folder nested deeper would not be covered.

followUps.name: One resolver for the three folders
followUps.note: The documents publish resolves with `realpath -m`, the staging check resolves the text itself; for the live folders the two agree. Moving the documents publish onto the same function would leave one way of resolving them. The earlier follow-up of #8 for a regression check of the documents publish's target check stays open.

followUps.name: A shared step runner for the workflow tests
followUps.note: `StagingMarkingTest` and `StagingTargetCheckTest` each carry their own code that runs a step body in bash; a third step test is the moment to move it into `support/workflows`.
